newsitem.title: SENEGAL: W.African central bank praises local economies.
newsitem.headline: W.African central bank praises local economies.

text.p: The governor of the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) said on Friday that the bank was currently in a strong position, reflecting the economies of its member countries.

"The situation of the Central Bank has strengthened, improved considerably, which is a perfect reflection of the economic and financial situation of our states," Charles Konan Banny told a news conference in Dakar, where the BCEAO has its headquarters.
The member states, which form the western African part of the Franc Zone, are Burkina Faso, Benin, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo.
The BCEAO's foreign reserves stand at $3 billion. "This is the first time we have reached such an outstanding result," Banny said.
The common currency of the African Franc Zone states is linked to the French franc. It was devalued by 50 percent at the start of 1994.
Since then, economic growth had been positive, Banny said, although at first it was below the growth in the population.
"During the third year after the devaluation (1996), the growth rate reached 5.9 percent compared to a population growth of three percent," he said.

The governor praised the position of public finances in the eight member countries. "Public finances have become sounder and showed a surplus which will allow us by stages to finance investments," he said.
Guinea-Bissau became a member of the Franc Zone in May, and Banny said he would be very pleased if Gambia and Guinea, two other neighbouring countries, joined the monetary union.
"The earlier the better if Gambia and Guinea join other members of the union," he added.
